contract.note: Practical functionality and usefulness for the majority is an ordinary reading. Requiring more than feature availability fairly preserves the user qualification.

evidence.note: The original company announcement establishes the launch baseline. Its later introductory notice does not establish historical change.
The company disclosed new voice and image interactions within the target period. This counters the unchanged-functionality description but does not establish majority-user benefit.
The company disclosed broader access to tools beyond model substitutions. This is relevant counterevidence, without demonstrating actual use or material benefit for most users.

contract.note: The contract preserves the stated price and expansion goal without inventing a subscriber deadline. Treating product changes as proposed requirements rather than an external antecedent is reasonable.
